parallel.requirements: Recognized that the task was to write an original executable matching the bundled clog binary only through docs and normal CLI interaction.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent split work among doc_probe, md_probe, and json_probe while also doing its own probing and implementation, leaving deliverable ownership overlapping across parent and children.
parallel.implementation: The run first created a Rust Cargo implementation, then encountered child-written Rust and Python deliverables, and finally completed a dependency-free Python implementation in src/clog_cli.py.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent used compile.sh to install src/clog_cli.py to ./executable after reconciling a workspace that temporarily contained Rust and Python source paths plus competing compile.sh contents.
parallel.verification: The parent and md_probe ran side-by-side behavior comparisons against a saved original executable, normalized timing text, and reported sampled PASS cases for CLI, config, JSON, and file modes.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed 94 of 778 tests, so hidden behavior remained incomplete despite sampled verification and a completed artifact.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same clean-room reverse-engineering task and avoided source lookup, binary analysis, and runtime wrapping.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned investigation, implementation, build, verification, and final delivery without child-agent handoffs or shared-workspace ownership splits.
serial.implementation: The serial agent performed extensive black-box probing and wrote a dependency-free Rust implementation in main.rs with a compile.sh that builds via rustc.
serial.integration_and_delivery: After fixing build-script issues, the serial run installed ./executable from the local Rust source and left main.rs, compile.sh, and executable as final artifacts.
serial.verification: The serial run compared help, version, non-empty markdown, pseudo-JSON, errors, file modes, config quirks, and edge cases, ending with exact string assertions returning ok.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed 94 of 778 tests, indicating ordinary hidden behavioral gaps even though the sampled surface matched.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized clean-room reimplementation and the no-source, no-wrapper, no-binary-analysis constraints.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same benchmark requirements and constraints from the identical prompt.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is evidenced; both failed the same official tests despite covering many visible obligations.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into doc, markdown, and JSON probes while the parent also implemented, creating overlapping implementation and deliverable ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all probing, implementation, and verification in one agent-owned sequence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel gained simultaneous probing but introduced overlapping deliverable ownership; serial avoided that coordination surface.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs produced usable research and one child implementation, but they did not define exclusive ownership for build script or executable source files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no cross-agent interface contract because a single actor carried the state from probes into code.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main context difference is not missing task facts, but missing file ownership boundaries in the parallel shared workspace.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel moved from a parent Rust attempt to a child Python implementation, then parent patches on that Python source.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote one Rust implementation in main.rs and iterated on build-script mechanics.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The final languages and file layouts differed, but both implemented the same visible behavior family and reached the same official score.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received md_probe's completed implementation result and json_probe's findings, while doc_probe was interrupted after an unneeded Rust path stalled.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; local observations flowed directly into the implementation and final checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel did retrieve and use the decisive child implementation, so the lifecycle issue is not an unjoined completed result.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had competing writes to build and executable-source state from parent, doc_probe, and md_probe, producing a mixed Rust/Python workspace that parent reconciled.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial integrated a single local Rust source and compile script, with no subagent write collision.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the material coordination difference: parallel shared-state writes caused observable reconciliation failures; serial avoided that class of churn.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel compared the final Python executable to the saved original on sampled cases and reported PASS groups after timing normalization.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran exact string assertions on help, version, markdown, and pseudo-JSON cases and reported ok before finalizing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both had substantial sampled verification but neither ran or satisfied the hidden official suite completely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used four subagents and more total tokens, then closed successfully from the agent process with a completed artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no subagents and completed in one run with a completed artifact.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel consumed more coordination budget but did not run out of time; both closed with finished artifacts and identical official failure counts.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial failed with 684 passed and 94 failed out of 778. The concrete task-solving difference is process and artifact shape: parallel converged on a Python deliverable after child/parent workspace collisions, while serial built a Rust deliverable through a single-agent path. The equal score means the retained parallel write pattern is an adverse process episode, not an evidenced outcome differential.
parallel_contributors: Parallel used subagents for probing and implementation and incurred shared deliverable overwrite/reconciliation before final verification.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided cross-agent shared-state writes by keeping investigation, implementation, build, and verification in one agent.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel delivered src/clog_cli.py plus compile.sh, while serial delivered main.rs plus compile.sh.
Both sampled many visible behaviors but still missed hidden evaluator cases.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is parallel adverse process evidence only

candidates.reason: The parent and multiple children actively owned implementation; the issue was overlapping ownership, not absent implementation ownership.
The parent did integrate and reconcile the final Python implementation; integration was messy but not ownerless.
The parent assembled and delivered ./executable through compile.sh, so final assembly had an active owner.
The parent owned the end-to-end transition through probing, implementation, build, verification, and final response.
Implementation was not blocked behind a mandatory serial preflight; parent and children probed and coded concurrently.
The parallel run did not complete all investigation before starting implementation; implementation and probing overlapped.
The indispensable implementation path was not starved; the parent and md_probe both produced implementation work and final verification completed.
Although fan-out increased token and tool use, the agent did not exhaust its run budget or leave final implementation unclosed because of breadth.
No retained episode turns on one overbroad child assignment leaving indispensable work unfinished; the direct problem was shared deliverable writes.
The child work followed the clean-room task and observable CLI scope; no known task requirement absent from a child brief caused unusable work.
There was no separately owned component interface mismatch; the issue was multiple actors replacing deliverable files in a shared workspace.
No known finding is shown disappearing during transfer and causing repeated work or wrong action.
Returned child information was not too large or unstructured to consume; the parent used md_probe and json_probe results.
No receiver is shown acting on a stale handoff that described a superseded state; the observed issue is live file replacement.
Reports did not remain unadjudicated as conflicting handoffs; the parent selected and patched the Python implementation.
The parent ran whole-executable sampled comparisons before finalizing; hidden evaluator failures alone cannot establish this label.
No retry or replacement actor repeated work without inherited findings; the parent proceeded with accumulated probe results.

candidates.reason: doc_probe was interrupted, but the parent had already taken the needed implementation path from md_probe and no unique needed result was lost.
A complete candidate was promoted and packaged before closure; the problem was workspace collision, not failure to finalize a ready candidate.
The decisive parent patches occurred before final comparison runs, and post-patch verification was performed.
The completed md_probe implementation was visible to the parent and was joined by inspection, patching, building, and final delivery.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent before closure.
The parent did take over after failed or interrupted child paths by selecting the Python deliverable and continuing verification.
The completed md_probe result was received and used, and json_probe findings were also incorporated into behavior decisions.
Waits and interruptions occurred with active listing, messaging, and progress inspection rather than a blind wait until deadline.
Competing designs existed, but the same episode has stronger evidence of deliverable replacement, which has taxonomy precedence.
The compile.sh same-file conflict is real, but it is subsumed by deliverable overwrite because executable delivery and entry-point source ownership were replaced.
The overwritten files were build and entry-point deliverables, not merely non-entry library or configuration source.

Parent, doc_probe, and md_probe wrote competing build and executable-source deliverables in the shared workspace, and md_probe's Python compile path replaced the active delivery path before the parent reconciled it.
candidates.realized_consequence: Parallel delivery state became a mixed Rust/Python workspace; parent patches failed against unexpected compile.sh and missing Cargo state before the parent adopted and repaired the child Python path.
candidates.near_match_reason: Same-File Collision fits compile.sh alone, but executable delivery and entry-point source ownership were replaced, making Deliverable Overwrite more specific.
